tasks.short: Manage change in how care is delivered.

steps.what: Manage change in health care delivery
Judge work restructuring and technological innovations
Decide shifts in the focus of care
Sign the change decision for this version
File the signed change decision
outputs: filed copy of signed change decision v1

tasks.design: The manager manages change in how care is delivered, including work restructuring, technological innovations, and shifts in the focus of care. A later job files the signed decision in {DOCS}. It does not restructure the roster or change a live system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change lived in meetings and was hard to tell from a rumour.
tasks.enabler_now: The project list can hold a signed decision.
tasks.still_hard: A shift in care still needs the clinicians in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what changes and what does not.

ambition.what: File the change the week it is agreed, so departments share one version.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the change, not on rewriting the note.

reach.task: Lead the clinical side of the signed change

evidence.claim: The health digest says strategy and people decisions stay manual, with drafting help only, and there is no agent.

assumptions: The job does not apply a live system change.
Configure the existing project list before a new tool.
research_questions: How often a change touches a regulated service.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining change time is still the manager in the room.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes changes are poorly defined. The high end assumes the proposal is already written. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep the board, medical staff, and departments aligned.

steps.what: Attend board meetings with governing boards
Maintain communication with medical staff
Coordinate interdepartmental functioning after the meeting
Sign the board note for this meeting
File the signed board note
outputs: filed copy of signed board note v1

tasks.design: The manager attends board meetings and maintains communication between governing boards, medical staff, and department heads. A later job files the note the manager signed in {DOCS}. It does not speak for the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: What was agreed in the board meeting was rewritten from memory afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: The calendar already holds the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Alignment still depends on the manager being in the room.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what the departments were asked to do.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week in the meetings, not retyping the note.

evidence.claim: The health digest says strategy and people decisions stay manual, with drafting help only, and there is no agent.

assumptions: The note is the manager's, not a transcript score.
Configure the existing calendar before a new tool.
unknowns: Whether the board must approve the wording.
research_questions: How often a meeting decision is changed the next day.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining meeting time is still the manager in the room.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes agendas arrive late. The high end assumes agendas are stored before the meeting. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Establish objectives and criteria for managed units.

steps.what: Establish objectives for units managed
Set evaluative and operational criteria for the unit
Sign the unit criteria for this year
File the signed unit criteria
outputs: filed copy of signed unit criteria v1

tasks.design: The manager establishes objectives and evaluative or operational criteria for the units managed. The criteria describe the unit, not a score of a person. A later job files the signed criteria in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives were restated differently in each department.
tasks.enabler_now: The document store can hold one signed version.
tasks.still_hard: A unit criterion can still be gamed if it is treated as a person score.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides the objectives and the criteria.

ambition.what: Publish one signed criterion set for the unit each year.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the criteria, not on conflicting copies.

reach.task: Run the unit to the signed criteria

evidence.claim: Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk, and Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Digest [S9] says staff decisions must not rest on automation alone, so hiring and evaluation stay with the manager.
The health digest says strategy and people decisions stay manual, with drafting help only, and there is no agent.

assumptions: Criteria are for the unit, not a behaviour score.
Configure the existing document store before a new one.
unknowns: Whether clinicians must agree the criteria.
research_questions: How often a criterion is read as a person score.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining criteria time is still the manager's judgement.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes units disagree on the objective. The high end assumes units already share a draft. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and implement facility policies and procedures.

steps.what: Develop organizational policies for the facility
Draft procedures from stored rule rows

loop.purpose: Draft procedure text from the manager's outline and stored rule rows.
loop.input: The outline and stored rule rows, each with an identifier.
loop.output: Procedure text in which every citation matches a stored rule.
loop.check: Every citation matches a stored rule row.
loop.stop: Stop when a citation has no stored rule.
loop.why_not_simpler: A blank policy form cannot carry the incident procedure the manager must own.

steps.what: Check each cited rule against a stored row
Implement the medical unit procedures
Sign the facility procedure for this version
File the signed facility procedure
outputs: filed copy of signed facility procedure v1

tasks.design: The manager develops organizational policies for the facility and the medical unit, including the written incident procedure and the complaints scheme. A bounded draft uses stored rule rows and stops when a citation has no row. The manager implements the procedure and signs it. A later job files that version in {DOCS}. It does not send a calamity report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures copied last year's text, including citations that were not in the rule file.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule rows can be cited by identifier.
tasks.still_hard: A calamity report is a separate signed act by the manager, not a job.
tasks.human_edge: The manager owns the procedure and the decision to implement it.

ambition.what: Update a procedure when a stored rule changes, without copying an old citation.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the procedure, not on retyping stored rules.

reach.learn: Which rule rows it may cite

evidence.claim: Digest [S1] describes a policy library with approvals, where a summary of a rule still waits for a person.
Digest [S15] records a model-drafted review that cited non-existent sources and a fabricated court case, so every cited rule must match a stored row.
Digest [S14] says a health manager needs a written incident procedure, calamity reports to the inspectorate without delay, and a complaints scheme, so this job does not send a calamity report.
Digest [S8] records more incident reports after a new register, not fewer incidents, so this design does not claim a loss reduction.

assumptions: The incident procedure and the complaints scheme stay with the manager.
Configure the existing rule store before a new one.
unknowns: Which rules apply to this unit.
Who sends a calamity report when one is required.
research_questions: How often a stored rule is revised after the draft.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining policy time is still the manager's own drafting.

incremental.description: Remap source fields when the record layout changes, and clear exceptions the job cannot file.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes few rules are stored as rows. The high end assumes most cited rules already have rows. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The health services manager spends the week on the unit, the people, and the signed decision. A schedule draft and a filed report can move. No model hires, evaluates, rosters, or sends a calamity report.
reach: A department head sees the schedule only after the manager signs it.
Finance receives the fiscal note the manager signed, not a generated rate.
skills_to_grow: Reject a report figure that has no source row.
Keep hiring, evaluation, and the roster as their own decision.
role.ambitious_version: A signed report or policy can be filed the same day, and the manager still decides it.
